exposure: no (or late first; >16 weeks) antenatal visit
pregnancy complications (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia)
outcome: mental disorder diagnoses (up to age 13-14 years)
substantiated childhood maltreatment (up to age 13-14 years)
contact with the police as a victim (up to age 13-14 years)
contact with the police as a person-of-interest (up to age 13-14 years)
cohort: The study included 72,059 Australian children and their parents from a multi-register population cohort study with data spanning 1994-2018.
finding: Risk exposures evident at birth predicted individual childhood outcomes, including developmental vulnerability, educational underachievement, mental disorder, substantiated maltreatment, and police contact, with fair to excellent accuracy up to age 13-14 years.
